info.title: AI Native Call Center API
info.summary: REST and SSE surface of the AI-native call center.
info.description:
The single contract for every HTTP endpoint the platform serves. Spec-first: this document is the source of truth; Go and TypeScript types are generated from it, never the other way around.

Naming follows docs/design/07-naming.md: JSON properties are lowerCamelCase with initialisms treated as words (callId), enum values are SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and byte-identical across JSON, TypeScript and the database, timestamps are xxxAt (RFC 3339), durations are xxxSec/xxxMs, booleans are is/has prefixed.

Authentication is an HttpOnly session cookie issued by POST /auth/login. Every mutating request must also carry the X-AICC-Csrf header with any non-empty value. Errors always use the single envelope {"error": {code, message, params}}; the code is machine-readable and localized by the frontend.

A separate unauthenticated operations listener (AICC_METRICS_ADDR, default 127.0.0.1:9090) serves GET /metrics, /healthz and /readyz in plain text; it is deliberately outside this contract.

Server-sent events, one SseEvent envelope per data: line, the type mirrored on the event: line and the global seq on the id: line. Scope comes from the authenticated identity; ?types= may only narrow what that identity would already receive. Reconnection resumes from Last-Event-ID (or ?lastEventId=); a resume point older than the replay ring triggers a SYSTEM_RESET event telling the client to refetch snapshots. A comment heartbeat (": hb") flows every 15 seconds. The connection has no timeout; it ends with the client.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Comma-separated SseEventType names to narrow the stream.

parameters.name: lastEventId
parameters.description: Resume point for clients that cannot set the Last-Event-ID header.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The browser's own resume point, echoed from the id: line.

200.description: The stream. Each data: line is one SseEvent; per-type payload shapes live in components/schemas under the Sse*Payload naming convention (SseCallbackEventPayload, SseSystemResetPayload).

cookieSession.name: aicc_session
cookieSession.description: Opaque session token issued by POST /auth/login. The cookie name is configurable (AICC_SESSION_COOKIE); aicc_session is the default. HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax.

csrfHeader.name: X-AICC-Csrf
csrfHeader.description: Anti-CSRF header required on every mutating request (any method other than GET, HEAD, OPTIONS). Any non-empty value passes; requiring a custom header forces a CORS preflight on cross-origin callers. Missing header: 403 FORBIDDEN.

BadRequest.description: The request is malformed: unparseable body or an invalid identifier. Code VALIDATION_FAILED.

Unauthorized.description: No session or the session expired. Codes SESSION_EXPIRED, INVALID_CREDENTIALS.

Forbidden.description: The identity lacks the role, the CSRF header is missing, the account is suspended, or the account is not an agent. Codes FORBIDDEN, USER_SUSPENDED, NOT_CALL_PARTY.

NotFound.description: The target does not exist. Codes NOT_FOUND, CALL_NOT_FOUND.

Conflict.description: The request collides with current state. Codes CONFLICT, EXTENSION_IN_USE, EXTENSION_ASSIGNED_TO_AGENT, AGENT_ALREADY_LOGGED_IN, AGENT_NOT_LOGGED_IN, AGENT_NOT_IN_WRAP_UP.

UnprocessableEntity.description: The body parsed but a field is missing or invalid. Code VALIDATION_FAILED; params.field names the offender when known.

BadGateway.description: The switch did not take the call. Code SWITCH_DOWN.

ServiceUnavailable.description: A dependency is unreachable. Codes STORAGE_DOWN, SWITCH_DOWN.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable, translatable failure identifier. The frontend renders errors.<CODE>; the backend never localizes.

Error.description: The single error envelope body: an error code plus interpolation params. Message is diagnostic English, never shown to end users.

params.description: Interpolation parameters for the localized message, e.g. {"field": "extensionNumber"}.

Role.description: Ranked roles; a higher role passes every lower gate (ADMIN > SUPERVISOR > AGENT).

locale.description: Preferred UI locale (lowercase BCP 47 subtag) or null when the user has not chosen one.

NotReadyReason.description: Why an agent is NOT_READY. LOGIN, AFTER_CALL_WORK, SYSTEM and SUPERVISOR are set by the platform, never chosen by the agent.

Availability.description: The single word that answers: could this agent take a call, and if not, why.

Presence.description: One agent's presence. enteredAt is when this state began, which for WRAP_UP is when the call ended — after-call work has no deadline, it ends when the agent files it.

agentId.description: Whose presence this is. The cockpit needs it to tell its own party from the other side on a call where both parties are agents — an internal extension-to-extension call reaches both of them through /calls/mine, and picking the first party that happens to carry an agentId shows one agent the other one's state.

wrapUpCallId.description: The call the agent is doing after-call work for. Set while availability is WRAP_UP and kept until the next call is wrapped, so a filing made after the agent has moved on still lands on the right call.

WrapUpRequest.description: What the agent confirms for the call they just finished. Both fields are optional: the record already exists with a default disposition, and pressing Done with neither is an agent saying the defaults are right.

dispositionCode.description: A code from GET /dispositions; omitted keeps the one on the record.

note.description: Omitted keeps the note on the record.

CurrentWrapUp.description: The after-call work waiting on this agent: the record the platform opened for the call they just finished, as it stands. It survives a page reload, which is how a cockpit knows to keep asking.

createdAt.description: When after-call work began for this call.

AgentLoginRequest.description: Sign-in takes no arguments in the ordinary case: the agent-to-extension binding is static configuration, so the platform signs the agent in at the phone they are bound to.

extensionNumber.description: Overrides the bound extension. Omit it to use the agent's configured phone; an agent with no binding is refused with CONFLICT.

reason.description: Omitted or empty defaults to BREAK.

RosterEntry.description: One agent on the supervisor roster.

extensionNumber.description: The phone the agent is signed in at right now; absent when signed out.

callcenterName.description: The identifier the switch knows this agent by.

defaultExtensionId.description: The extension bound to this agent in configuration. Unlike extensionNumber it survives sign-out, and it is what administration edits.

defaultExtensionNumber.description: The bound extension's number, resolved for display.

Agent.description: One agent's configuration, as administration stores it. Presence is not part of it — the roster carries that.

userId.description: The account this agent identity belongs to. One user has at most one agent identity.

AgentWrite.description: Create or update an agent identity. An extension may be bound to at most one agent; binding one that is taken is refused with CONFLICT.

userId.description: Required on create and ignored on update: an agent identity never moves between accounts.

callcenterName.description: Reaches the switch as an identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

defaultExtensionId.description: The phone this agent signs in at. Null unbinds them, after which they cannot sign in.

User.description: An account, as the agent editor needs to name it.

CallType.description: Caller-perspective call type, stamped at creation and immutable across transfers.

PartySnapshot.description: Immutable view of one call leg.

isMuted.description: True while the switch is silencing this leg's microphone.

QueueFacts.description: A call's passage through a queue.

CallSnapshot.description: Immutable view of a live call: the aggregate plus its parties.

userData.description: Business data attached to the call; merge-patched, survives transfers.

WaitingCall.description: A caller waiting in a queue: joined and not yet bridged to anybody. Ordered longest wait first, which is who the queue serves next.

slaThresholdSec.description: The queue's answer target; a wait past it is a breach. 0 means none is configured.

digits.description: The tones to emit, in order. 0-9, A-D, * and # are the only DTMF symbols there are.

destination.description: The number to call once the agent's own leg answers.

CreateCallRequest.description: Ask the platform to place a call. AI_OUTBOUND is the only kind so far.

callId.description: Client-minted id making the request idempotent: a retry with the same id answers isDuplicate instead of redialing.

did.description: The DID whose flow and caller id the call uses.

language.description: Overrides the DID's language when set.

isDuplicate.description: Present and true when the client-minted callId was already placed; the response points at the existing call.

Extension.description: A SIP endpoint the switch will accept a registration for.

ExtensionWrite.description: Create or update an extension. Omitted fields take server defaults (kind AGENT, displayName "Extension <number>", isEnabled true).

password.description: Write-only: required on create, optional on update (empty keeps the current one). Never returned; the only reader that needs it is the switch.

Strategy.description: How a queue picks among the agents staffing it, in platform vocabulary; the switch spelling is a boundary translation.

Overflow.description: Where an unserved caller goes. BOT_FLOW and FORWARD need a target.

TierRules.description: How a queue widens its agent search over time.

Queue.description: A waiting line served by agents.

name.description: Switch-safe identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

QueueWrite.description: Create or update a queue. Omitted fields take server defaults (strategy LONGEST_IDLE_AGENT, overflow ANNOUNCE_HANGUP, mohSound $${hold_music}, tierRules.waitSec 300, isEnabled true, isRecordingEnabled true).

name.description: Switch-safe identifier: no spaces, @ or quotes.

QueueAgent.description: One agent's place on a queue.

DID.description: An external number that reaches this call centre. Every number is meant to answer with a bot flow; the fallback queue takes the caller when the bot cannot.

language.description: Lowercase BCP 47 subtag, at most 8 characters. Sets the greeting, the prompt language and the voice; it does not select a provider, which is a deployment-wide setting.

DIDWrite.description: Create or update a DID. Omitted fields take server defaults (language en, isEnabled true, isRecordingEnabled true).

CDRStatus.description: How the call concluded. There is no MISSED status: abandonment is a missedReason on an ANSWERED row, because the bot answered first.

Leg.description: One hop of the call's journey, for the journey summary.

CDR.description: One finished call. totalSec always equals the sum of its parts.

answeredAt.description: When the call became billable: the moment the leg facing whoever charges for it was answered. Inbound, that is the caller's own leg and the 200 OK the switch sent towards the carrier; on a call an agent placed it is the leg dialled out, since the agent's own phone picks up in front of them and nobody bills for that. Set even on a call the bot served and no agent took, which is billed all the same. Between two extensions it records the answer while billSec stays 0.

ringSec.description: Seconds spent ringing an agent. For an answered call, from the answering leg's creation to its bridge; for one nobody answered, from the first leg dialled to the last one released — a queue that re-offers dials a fresh leg each time, so no single leg holds the answer.

botSec.description: Seconds the caller spent with the bot, ending when they actually left it — after any closing sentence has finished playing, not when the transfer was decided.

queueWaitSec.description: Seconds the caller waited in queue, from joining to being bridged to an agent, or to leaving if they never were. Ringing happens inside this window, so ringSec is a sub-interval of it rather than an addition to it.

talkSec.description: Seconds an agent had two-way media with the caller, measured from the bridges on the agent legs and unioned across them, so a call passed from one agent to another counts both stretches once. A leg that answered without a bridge — an auto-answer phone in front of nobody, a codec mismatch — contributes nothing. Hold counts as talk.

billSec.description: Billable seconds: answeredAt to endedAt. This is the carrier's number, not the agent's — a call the bot answered and nobody took is still billed. 0 when the call was never answered, and 0 between two extensions, which nobody charges for.

totalSec.description: Seconds from startedAt to endedAt, the whole life of the call including the time before it was answered. Not the billable duration; see billSec.

missedReason.description: Why the caller went unserved; empty when the call was not missed.

isContained.description: True when the bot finished the conversation without a human.

tech.description: Technical residue (switch causes and the like); never business data.

wrapUp.description: The after-call work filed for this call: the requesting agent's own on GET /cdrs/mine, the primary agent's (else the latest) elsewhere. Absent when nobody filed one.

WrapUp.description: One agent's after-call work for one call. The platform opens it when the call ends — a default disposition, an empty note — and the agent confirms it; isConfirmed is what separates a record somebody looked at from one nobody has. The label is captured at filing time so the record survives later edits to the vocabulary.

isConfirmed.description: True once the agent pressed Done. False means the defaults are still standing.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, for paging.

TranscriptLine.description: One thing said or done on a call, in either phase. seq is dense per call and is both the sort key and the backfill cursor.

content.description: TEXT carries {text}; TOOL_CALL and TOOL_RESULT carry the tool name and arguments or result.

Recording.description: One stored audio artifact of a call.

backend.description: Storage backend, e.g. fs or s3.

CDRDetail.description: One finished call with everything it left behind, in one round trip.

Callback.description: A promise to call somebody back, taken by the bot and kept by an agent.

handledBy.description: The user working or having closed the callback.

status.description: DONE means the promise was kept; DISMISSED means it no longer needs keeping.

Contact.description: A customer record. The phone number is the key the cockpit looks a caller up by, so it is unique.

lastCallAt.description: When this number last appeared on a finished call, either side. Absent when it never has.

ContactWrite.description: Create or update a contact. Omitted fields are stored empty on create and left unchanged on update.

total.description: Total rows matching the filter, for paging.

Disposition.description: One word an agent can file a call under. The code is stable; the label is what agents read and is the operator's to change.

DispositionCatalog.description: The wrap-up vocabulary: every enabled disposition, in display order.

QualityReview.description: A reviewer's scoring of one recording.

scores.description: Per-criterion scores; null when the reviewer submitted none.

Overview.description: KPI aggregates over the report window.

AgentToday.description: One agent's own day, over the window (default: local midnight to now). The totals are served beside the averages so every number on the screen can be checked against them.

callsHandled.description: Calls this agent answered, counted from the ledger's primary agent.

talkSec.description: Total talk time on those calls.

wrapUpSec.description: Total after-call work, from the presence history; an open wrap-up counts up to now.

signedInSec.description: Total time signed in, whatever the state; the denominator of occupancy.

avgHandleSec.description: (talkSec + wrapUpSec) / callsHandled — the average handle time. 0 when no call was handled.

avgWrapUpSec.description: wrapUpSec / the number of wrap-ups begun in the window. 0 when there were none.

occupancyPct.description: (talkSec + wrapUpSec) / signedInSec as a percentage, 0 when signed out all window.

wrapUpsOpened.description: After-call records opened in the window — one per call this agent finished.

wrapUpsConfirmed.description: How many of them the agent confirmed.

confirmedPct.description: wrapUpsConfirmed / wrapUpsOpened as a percentage — how much of the day's after-call work somebody actually looked at. 0 when nothing was opened.

queueId.description: Null aggregates the calls that never entered a queue.

oldestSeq.description: Oldest sequence still in the replay ring; a client behind it must resync.

SseEventType.description: Every event name on the stream. PARTY_* are leg-scoped, CALL_* call-scoped, SYSTEM_* stream-control.

SseEvent.description: One envelope on the event stream. Call events repeat enough context (callType, userData) for a screen-pop without further requests. In SSE framing the envelope is the data: line, the event: line carries type, and the id: line carries seq.

seq.description: Global order. Echo the last seen value as Last-Event-ID to resume.

payload.description: Type-specific body. Stable shapes are named Sse*Payload in this document; the rest are registered as they harden.

SseQueueJoinedPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_JOINED: a caller entered the queue named on the envelope's queueId.

SseQueueLeftPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_LEFT: the caller left the queue, whether answered, abandoned or timed out. cause and cancelReason are the queue's own words, stable codes rather than display text.

SseQueueCountPayload.description: Payload of QUEUE_COUNT: how many callers are waiting in the queue named on the envelope's queueId, published whenever that number moves.

longestWaitAt.description: When the longest-waiting caller joined; absent when nobody is waiting.

SseSystemResetPayload.description: Payload of SYSTEM_RESET: the resume point aged out of the ring; refetch snapshots before tailing again.

Speaker.description: Who said a line. CUSTOMER is the person who called, whichever leg carries them; BOT is the AI; HUMAN_AGENT is a logged-in agent answering after a transfer.

TranscriptSource.description: Where a line came from. MODEL is the conversational engine's own transcript of the AI leg; ASR is a separate recognition of streamed audio.

TranscriptionState.description: Health of live transcription for a call, as the agent should see it.

SseTranscriptPayload.description: Payload of CALL_TRANSCRIPT: one line of the conversation, from either phase of the call. seq orders the transcript within the call and is unrelated to the envelope's transport seq. A partial carries isFinal false and no seq, because it has no place in the order until it is final.

SseTranscriptionStatePayload.description: Payload of CALL_TRANSCRIPTION_STATE: whether the agent is seeing everything that is being said, and if not, which side is missing. reason is a stable code, never display text.

CallTranscript.description: A page of a call's transcript, plus where to resume. isLive says whether more is still coming, so a client knows to tail rather than poll.
